recordText: In English from 1883: a child prodigy, especially in music. From German *Wunderkind*, "wonder-child." The *wonder* half goes back to Old English *wundor*, a word of unknown origin.
gossipText: The prodigy. Half of her name is family; the other half has no known origin. She doesn't like to discuss it.
testimony: In German he's König. In Dutch, koning. Every one of them goes back to the same Germanic grandfather, kuningaz. I made a chart.

clue.summary: cyning ← Proto-Germanic kuningaz; cousins German König, Dutch koning
